bug_semantics: Authenticated ticket routes accepted a user-controlled numeric ticket id without constraining the selected Ticket to the authenticated user's company_id. GET /ticket/update/{id} exposed another tenant's ticket content and, once attachment support existed, its attachments; POST /ticket/save loaded another tenant's Ticket and then reassigned company_id and saved it; GET /ticket/delete/{id} deleted an arbitrary Ticket while its generic Request type also bypassed TicketDeleteRequest authorization.
flaw_origin: Commit 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd is the smallest real BIC: it created the reachable ticket update and save routes and controllers with Ticket::find($id) and Ticket::find($request->id), respectively, without tenant scoping. Commit 946a0c5e43a1178534e5b013ea2608d565686220 later expanded the same object-ownership flaw to deletion, and 626b0228c248637086ce91bb17b2ec1b1c21961b later expanded read impact to attachments. Commit 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d merely moved the already-vulnerable save lookup into TicketRepository and is not an introducer.
evidence: The assigned advisory bundle says the flaw affects versions before 5.4.9 and directly references b2b6ffdace0972ab62d1f7e8cdab0ed213bfc4a9. `git show --format=fuller b2b6ffdace0972ab62d1f7e8cdab0ed213bfc4a9` confirms that this direct patch replaces all three unscoped selections with id-plus-authenticated-company queries ending in firstOrFail() and changes TicketDeleteController from generic Request to TicketDeleteRequest.

`git show --format=fuller 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd -- app/Http/Controllers/Ticket routes/web.php` shows a one-parent `Tickets CRUD` commit creating /ticket/update/{id} and /ticket/save along with new controllers containing Ticket::find($id) and Ticket::find($request->id); the save path then assigns Auth::user()->company_id. This is an original vulnerable implementation, not an aggregate, import, move, or refactor.

Direct-parent verification: `git cat-file commit 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd` gives the sole parent 063d713c71ca6c453d43e7b17a9ee2f8b2fc0ce1. `git ls-tree -r --name-only` on that parent for the ticket controllers, repository, and delete request returns no paths, and `git grep -n -i ticket` on the parent's routes/web.php returns no match. The reachable vulnerable handlers are therefore absent from the immediate parent.

`git show 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d -- app/Http/Controllers/Ticket/TicketSaveController.php app/Repositories/TicketRepository.php` removes the existing unscoped lookup from the controller and reproduces it in a new repository, rejecting that later move as a BIC. `git show 946a0c5e43a1178534e5b013ea2608d565686220` separately shows the later creation of the unscoped delete route and controller, while `git show 626b0228c248637086ce91bb17b2ec1b1c21961b` shows attachments added atop the already-unscoped update lookup.

Version-boundary verification: `git rev-parse b2b6ffdace0972ab62d1f7e8cdab0ed213bfc4a9^` returns 361566c1ddb01df16f2cff0aa836f04be174f3c4, whose version.php reports 5.4.8. The immediate follow-up 7e86b0845b14887b101a4516020fedafbff23564 changes version.php from 5.4.8 to 5.4.9 with subject `chore: update version after ticket security fixes`. `git tag --contains` the fix returns v5.5.3 and v5.14.0, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms the BIC precedes the fix.

The sole assigned disagreement was marker_state: the primary serialized an explanatory `absent — ...` string, while the reviewer serialized null. Re-running `git cat-file commit 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd` shows author and committer Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com>, one parent, and message exactly `Tickets CRUD`, with no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI signal. Accordingly the reviewer's null marker state is canonical; the primary's substantive observation is correct but its explanatory text belongs in evidence, not ai_marker. Claude attribution on the later fix and version bump is excluded because it is not present on the BIC commit object.
reasoning: Vulnerability-first tracing identifies the 2022 Tickets CRUD commit as the first commit that made attacker-selected ticket ids reachable for cross-tenant read and ownership-changing save; its direct parent has neither the handlers nor routes. Later delete and attachment commits broadened impact, while the repository extraction only moved existing vulnerable logic, so none supplants the smallest BIC and no squash decomposition is needed. The advisory-linked fix directly closes read, write, delete, and delete-request authorization, and the 5.4.8-to-5.4.9 boundary is verified. On the only disputed field, marker_state, both auditors agreed that the BIC object has no AI evidence, but only the reviewer represented absence canonically as null. The primary's non-null prose was not an AI marker. BIC-only attribution therefore resolves to NOT_AI, regardless of Claude trailers on later non-BIC commits.
